     2	# Moving-Throat PDE — Stage 114: Concrete Two-Channel Core Outlet Model
     3	
     4	## Goal
     5	
     6	Replace the reduced outlet coefficients `(\rho_R,\sigma_W,\kappa_W,\gamma_W)` by a concrete throat-core response model with explicit internal variables.
     7	
     8	## Core variables
     9	
    10	Let `u(\omega)` be the isotropic `l=2` mouth amplitude seen by the exterior branch. Introduce two internal core variables:
    11	
    12	- `s(\omega)`: a static geometric compliance coordinate,
    13	- `q(\omega)`: a mixed `A_w/F_{\mu w}`-type side-channel coordinate.
    14	
    15	Take the linear core system
    16	\[
    17	\begin{pmatrix}
    18	K_s & \lambda\\[2pt]
    19	\lambda & -K_q D_W^{\rm bare}(z)
    20	\end{pmatrix}
    21	\binom{s}{q}
    22	=
    23	u\binom{g_s}{g_q},
    24	\qquad
    25	z:=\frac{a\omega}{c_s},
    26	\]
    27	with bare mixed denominator
    28	\[
    29	D_W^{\rm bare}(z)=1-\kappa_0 z^2-i\gamma_0 z^5+O(z^6).
    30	\]
    31	The mouth feedback is defined by
    32	\[
    33	\delta\Lambda_{\rm core}(z)\,u = g_s s + g_q q.
    34	\]
    35	
    36	This is the simplest concrete isotropic core model that contains:
    37	- a static geometric compliance,
    38	- a dynamic mixed side-channel,
    39	- and a nontrivial static/mixed hybridization `\lambda`.
    40	
    41	## Exact Schur-complement outlet
    42	
    43	Eliminating `(s,q)` gives the exact core correction
    44	\[
    45	\boxed{
    46	\delta\Lambda_{\rm core}(z)
    47	=
    48	\frac{g_s^2}{K_s}
    49	-
    50	\frac{(K_s g_q-\lambda g_s)^2}
    51	{K_s\big(K_sK_q D_W^{\rm bare}(z)+\lambda^2\big)}.
    52	}
    53	\]
    54	
    55	Define the dimensionless hybridization ratio
    56	\[
    57	r_c:=\frac{\lambda^2}{K_sK_q}.
    58	\]
    59	Then the outlet takes the reduced Stage-112 form
    60	\[
    61	\boxed{
    62	\delta\Lambda_{\rm core}(z)
    63	=
    64	\rho_c
    65	-
    66	\frac{\sigma_c}{1-\kappa_c z^2-i\gamma_c z^5}
    67	+O(z^6),
    68	}
    69	\]
    70	with exact core-level identifications
    71	\[
    72	\boxed{
    73	\rho_c=\frac{g_s^2}{K_s},
    74	}
    75	\]
    76	\[
    77	\boxed{
    78	\sigma_c=
    79	\frac{(K_s g_q-\lambda g_s)^2}
    80	{K_s^2K_q(1+r_c)},
    81	}
    82	\]
    83	\[
    84	\boxed{
    85	\kappa_c=\frac{\kappa_0}{1+r_c},
    86	\qquad
    87	\gamma_c=\frac{\gamma_0}{1+r_c}.
    88	}
    89	\]
    90	
    91	So the concrete core model reproduces the full reduced Robin–mixed hybrid outlet with no extra assumptions.
    92	
    93	## Interpretation
    94	
    95	This is already a significant narrowing. The outlet is no longer described by four unrelated reduced coefficients. It is controlled by:
    96	
    97	- one static shell stiffness `K_s`,
    98	- one mixed-channel stiffness `K_q`,
    99	- one static/mixed hybridization `\lambda`,
   100	- and two mouth couplings `(g_s,g_q)`,
   101	- plus the bare mixed low-frequency pair `(\kappa_0,\gamma_0)`.
   102	
   103	The next question is whether this concrete core model can *naturally* land on the compensated canonical branch found algebraically in Stage 112.

research/pde_ledger/redteam/pass2/reports/stage_160.md:36:`δγ_W = (δγ_0 − δκ_0/3)/(1+𝔯_{F1}²)`. The notes derive this in three logical steps: (1) the exact compensated-branch identity `δγ_W − (1/3)δκ_W = (δγ_0 − (1/3)δκ_0)/(1+r_{c,*})`, in which the `δr_c` dependence cancels identically; (2) under the Stage-159 canonical-even gate `δκ_W = 0` this collapses to `δγ_W = (δγ_0 − δκ_0/3)/(1+r_{c,*})`; (3) pure-scale harmlessness — if `δγ_0 = δκ_0/3` then `δγ_W = 0` (hence `Δ_Q = 0`, `N_Q−1 = 0`). The notes then push to the final defect law `Δ_Q = −9σ_*Υ_Π/[(1−σ_*)(1+𝔯_{F1}²)]·δΠ_tan` (and `N_Q−1` with `+`), with the tangential transport `δΠ_tan = 0.832409471081635 δΣ_0 − 1.16275838754222 δS`.      2	# Moving-Throat PDE — Stage 117: Concrete Outlet-Core Status
     3	
     4	The outlet-deformation problem is now much narrower.
     5	
     6	## What is now explicit
     7	
     8	The isotropic outlet is no longer described by four reduced coefficients
     9	\[
    10	(\rho_R,\sigma_W,\kappa_W,\gamma_W).
    11	\]
    12	In the first concrete core model it is generated by:
    13	
    14	- a static shell compliance `K_s`,
    15	- a mixed-channel stiffness `K_q`,
    16	- a static/mixed hybridization `\lambda`,
    17	- mouth couplings `(g_s,g_q)`,
    18	- and an auxiliary mixed D/N tube of length `L_W`.
    19	
    20	The exact eliminated outlet is
    21	\[
    22	\delta\Lambda_{\rm core}(z)
    23	=
    24	\rho_c-\frac{\sigma_c}{1-\kappa_c z^2-i\gamma_c z^5},
    25	\]
    26	with explicit formulas derived in Stages 114–116.
    27	
    28	## What preserves the canonical outgoing branch
    29	
    30	The concrete outlet lands exactly on the nontrivial compensated branch iff
    31	
    32	\[
    33	g_s^2(K_sK_q+\lambda^2)=4(K_sg_q-\lambda g_s)^2,
    34	\]
    35	\[
    36	L_W=\frac{\pi a}{2}\sqrt{\frac{1+r_c}{3}},
    37	\qquad
    38	r_c=\frac{\lambda^2}{K_sK_q},
    39	\]
    40	and the bare mixed outlet is a pure-scale deformation of the canonical compact outgoing `l=2` branch.
    41	
    42	On that surface the full outlet reduces to
    43	\[
    44	\Lambda_{\rm eff}(z)
    45	=
    46	\Lambda_2^{\rm out}(z)
    47	+
    48	4\sigma_*-\frac{\sigma_*}{1-z^2/3-i z^5/9},
    49	\qquad
    50	\sigma_*=\frac{g_s^2}{4K_s},
    51	\]
    52	which preserves
    53	\[
    54	\widehat Y_2(z)=1+\frac{z^2}{9}+\frac{4z^4}{81}+i\frac{z^5}{27}+O(z^6).
    55	\]
    56	
    57	## What remains open
    58	
    59	So the surviving PDE-facing question is no longer “is there some deformed outlet?”
    60	It is much sharper:
    61	
    62	> Does the actual moving-throat core realize the concrete coupling-balance surface and the auxiliary D/N-tube normalization identified above?
    63	
    64	That is a genuinely microscopic throat-core question, not more reduced outlet algebra.

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""
     3	Stage 105 SymPy audit.
     4	
     5	Provenance notes
     6	----------------
     7	- `Omega_Q = 3 c_s / (2 a)` is the same minimal-isotropic pole scale fixed by
     8	  the Stage 088 conservative quadrupole module.
     9	- `sigma_Q^can = 4 a^5 / (27 c_s^5)` is the canonical outgoing `l=2` DtN odd
    10	  coefficient inherited from the Stage 104 exact fingerprint.
    11	"""
    12	
    13	from __future__ import annotations
    14	import sympy as sp
    15	
    16	def banner(title: str) -> None:
    17	    line = "=" * 88
    18	    print("\n" + line)
    19	    print(title)
    20	    print(line)
    21	
    22	def expect_zero(name: str, expr: sp.Expr) -> None:
    23	    expr = sp.simplify(sp.expand(expr))
    24	    print(f"{name} = {expr}")
    25	    if expr != 0:
    26	        raise AssertionError(f"{name} is not zero")
    27	
    28	banner("STAGE 105 — EXACT FIXING OF chi_Q")
    29	
    30	a, c_s, omega, chi_Q = sp.symbols("a c_s omega chi_Q", positive=True, real=True)
    31	# Stage 088 minimal isotropic pole scale, carried into the retarded lane.
    32	Omega_Q = sp.simplify(3*c_s/(2*a))
    33	sigma_can = sp.simplify(sp.Rational(9, 8) / Omega_Q**5)
    34	
    35	print("Omega_Q =", Omega_Q)
    36	print("sigma_Q^can =", sigma_can)
    37	expect_zero("sigma_Q^can - 4 a^5/(27 c_s^5)", sigma_can - 4*a**5/(27*c_s**5))
    38	
    39	Yret = sp.Rational(3, 4) + sp.Rational(1, 4) / (1 - omega**2/Omega_Q**2 - sp.I*chi_Q*sigma_can*omega**5)
    40	Yret_series = sp.expand(sp.series(Yret, omega, 0, 6).removeO())
    41	
    42	print("\nY_Q^ret(omega) =")
    43	sp.pprint(Yret_series)
    44	
    45	expect_zero("omega^2 coefficient", Yret_series.coeff(omega, 2) - a**2/(9*c_s**2))
    46	expect_zero("omega^4 coefficient", Yret_series.coeff(omega, 4) - 4*a**4/(81*c_s**4))
    47	expect_zero("imag omega^5 coefficient", Yret_series.coeff(omega, 5)/sp.I - chi_Q*a**5/(27*c_s**5))
    48	
    49	z_out = sp.symbols("z", real=True)
    50	j2_out = (sp.Integer(3)/z_out**3 - 1/z_out)*sp.sin(z_out) - 3*sp.cos(z_out)/z_out**2
    51	y2_out = -((sp.Integer(3)/z_out**3 - 1/z_out)*sp.cos(z_out) + 3*sp.sin(z_out)/z_out**2)
    52	h2_out = sp.simplify(j2_out + sp.I*y2_out)
    53	Lambda_out = sp.simplify(z_out * sp.diff(h2_out, z_out) / h2_out)
    54	Lambda_out_series = sp.expand(sp.series(Lambda_out, z_out, 0, 6).removeO())
    55	Lambda_out_expected = sp.expand(
    56	    -3 + z_out**2/sp.Integer(3) + z_out**4/sp.Integer(9) + sp.I*z_out**5/sp.Integer(9)
    57	)
    58	print("\nLambda_2^out(z) from exact h_2^(1) =")
    59	sp.pprint(Lambda_out_series)
    60	expect_zero("Lambda_2^out series fingerprint", Lambda_out_series - Lambda_out_expected)
    61	
    62	Y_out = sp.simplify(sp.Integer(-3) / Lambda_out)
    63	Y_out_series = sp.expand(sp.series(Y_out, z_out, 0, 6).removeO())
    64	outgoing_z5_coeff = sp.simplify(Y_out_series.coeff(z_out, 5) / sp.I)
    65	expect_zero("Y_2^out imag z^5 coefficient - 1/27", outgoing_z5_coeff - sp.Rational(1, 27))
    66	outgoing_omega5_coeff = sp.simplify(outgoing_z5_coeff * (a/c_s)**5)
    67	
    68	chi_sol = sp.solve(sp.Eq(Yret_series.coeff(omega, 5)/sp.I, outgoing_omega5_coeff), chi_Q)[0]
    69	print("\nchi_Q from exact outgoing match =", chi_sol)
    70	if sp.simplify(chi_sol - 1) != 0:
    71	    raise AssertionError("chi_Q did not match to 1.")
    72	
    73	# General deformed DtN coefficient xi_Q.
    74	z, xi_Q = sp.symbols("z xi_Q", real=True)
    75	Lam_def = -3 + z**2/sp.Integer(3) + z**4/sp.Integer(9) + sp.I*xi_Q*z**5/sp.Integer(9)
    76	Y_def = sp.expand(sp.series(sp.Integer(-3)/Lam_def, z, 0, 6).removeO())
    77	print("\nDeformed DtN normalized branch =")
    78	sp.pprint(Y_def)
    79	
    80	expect_zero("deformed z^2 coefficient", Y_def.coeff(z, 2) - sp.Rational(1, 9))
    81	expect_zero("deformed z^4 coefficient", Y_def.coeff(z, 4) - sp.Rational(4, 81))
    82	expect_zero("deformed imag z^5 coefficient", Y_def.coeff(z, 5)/sp.I - xi_Q/sp.Integer(27))
    83	
    84	print("\nRESULT:")
    85	print("  On the canonical compact passive/outgoing grouped-P2 branch, chi_Q = 1 exactly.")
    86	print("  More generally, chi_Q is just the leading imaginary DtN deformation coefficient xi_Q.")

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""
     3	Stage 100 SymPy audit: outgoing-normalization factorization mhat_0^2 chi_Q N_Q = 1.
     4	
     5	Carry-forward annotations (per [[batch-IV1-paper-alignment]] Cluster B direction
     6	(c)): paper card `\\stagefield{Checks}` items
     7	  (ii) "higher odd terms begin beyond the point-particle 2.5PN coefficient"
     8	       — verified at stage 102 (higher_odd_irrelevance) via omega^7 series
     9	       extension and the tauQ-derivative gate; this stage's series truncates
    10	       at omega^5 by design.
    11	  (iii) "outgoing l=2 DtN fingerprint against the normalized z=omega a/c_s
    12	       expansion" — stage 104 proves the exact outgoing fingerprint, and stage
    13	       105 (chiQ_fix_from_outgoing_dtn) identifies chi_Q = 1 by DtN coefficient
    14	       matching. Both are downstream of this stage, so this stage carries chi_Q
    15	       as a free real symbol.
    16	This stage owns Check (i) — the `mhat_0^2 chi_Q N_Q = 1` closure — which is
    17	derived below by imposing the observable-side condition `mhat_0^2 * Gamma_5 =
    18	Gamma_5_target` on the script-derived Gamma_5(K_0, chi_Q, Omega).
    19	"""
    20	from __future__ import annotations
    21	import sympy as sp
    22	
    23	G, c = sp.symbols('G c', positive=True, real=True)
    24	Omega = sp.symbols('Omega', positive=True, real=True)
    25	K0, mhat0 = sp.symbols('K0 mhat0', positive=True, real=True)
    26	# chi_Q is a free real parameter at this stage. Its pinning to 1 by the l=2
    27	# DtN coefficient match is deferred downstream to stage 105, after the exact
    28	# outgoing fingerprint is proved at stage 104. Declaring it positive would
    29	# falsely constrain the factorization assertion below.
    30	chiQ = sp.symbols('chiQ', real=True)
    31	NQ = sp.symbols('N_Q', positive=True, real=True)
    32	omega = sp.symbols('omega', real=True)
    33	
    34	sigma_can = sp.Rational(9, 8) / Omega**5
    35	Y = sp.Rational(3,4) + sp.Rational(1,4) / (1 - omega**2/Omega**2 - sp.I*chiQ*sigma_can*omega**5)
    36	Yser = sp.expand(sp.series(Y, omega, 0, 6).removeO())
    37	
    38	K2 = sp.simplify(K0 * Yser.coeff(omega, 2))
    39	K4 = sp.simplify(K0 * Yser.coeff(omega, 4))
    40	Gamma5 = sp.simplify(sp.im(Yser.coeff(omega, 5)) * K0)
    41	
    42	K0_t = sp.simplify(64*G*Omega**5/(45*c**5))
    43	K2_t = sp.simplify(K0_t/(4*Omega**2))
    44	K4_t = sp.simplify(K0_t/(4*Omega**4))
    45	Gamma5_t = sp.simplify(2*G/(5*c**5))
    46	NQ_derived = sp.simplify(K0 / K0_t)
    47	
    48	print('Yhat_Q^ret series =', Yser)
    49	print('K2 =', K2)
    50	print('K4 =', K4)
    51	print('Gamma5 =', Gamma5)
    52	print('NQ =', NQ_derived)
    53	print('K2/K2_target - NQ =', sp.simplify(K2/K2_t - NQ_derived))
    54	print('K4/K4_target - NQ =', sp.simplify(K4/K4_t - NQ_derived))
    55	print('Gamma5/Gamma5_target - chiQ*NQ =', sp.simplify(Gamma5/Gamma5_t - chiQ*NQ_derived))
    56	assert sp.simplify(K2/K2_t - NQ_derived) == 0
    57	assert sp.simplify(K4/K4_t - NQ_derived) == 0
    58	assert sp.simplify(Gamma5/Gamma5_t - chiQ*NQ_derived) == 0
    59	
    60	# Substantive closure: impose the observable-side condition
    61	#   mhat_0^2 * Gamma_5 = Gamma_5_target
    62	# (the point-particle 2.5PN coefficient with source-map factor mhat_0^2 matches
    63	# the GR target). Substituting the script-derived Gamma_5 = chi_Q N_Q Gamma_5_target,
    64	# the residual factorizes as Gamma_5_target * (mhat_0^2 chi_Q N_Q - 1).
    65	# This is non-tautological because if the series derivation of Gamma_5 had a
    66	# wrong factor, the ratio below would not equal (mhat_0^2 chi_Q N_Q - 1).
    67	closure_residual = sp.simplify(mhat0**2 * Gamma5 - Gamma5_t)
    68	closure_ratio = sp.simplify(closure_residual / Gamma5_t)
    69	closure_check = sp.simplify(closure_ratio - (mhat0**2 * chiQ * NQ_derived - 1))
    70	print('closure_residual / Gamma5_target =', closure_ratio)
    71	print('closure_ratio - (mhat0^2 chi_Q N_Q - 1) =', closure_check)
    72	assert closure_check == 0
    73	
    74	# Headline ledger entry: on the closure (mhat_0^2 Gamma_5 = Gamma_5_target),
    75	# the factorization mhat_0^2 chi_Q N_Q = 1 is forced.
    76	print('\nClosure ledger: mhat_0^2 * Gamma_5 = Gamma_5_target  <=>  mhat_0^2 chi_Q N_Q = 1')
    77	print('STAGE 100 AUDIT PASSED')

research/pde_ledger/paper/appendices/reproducibility_map.tex:8:This appendix specifies how the derivation companion is to be checked.  The companion is not a single proof written in one style.  It is a layered verification record: some statements are exact identities of the parent action, some are exact algebra inside a declared closure, some are controlled reductions, some are finite search or numerical-location statements, and some remain open branch-realization targets.  The purpose of this map is to keep those layers auditable without weakening or overstating any claim.

   250	A framework succeeds when the derivation reduces a complicated PDE branch question to a finite, explicit packet of branch observables.  For example, reducing the retarded quadrupole finish line to \(\widehat m_0^{\,2}P_0\), or reducing the weak-axisymmetric obstruction to \(\Xi_1=P_1/P_0\), is a framework success even before an actual branch has returned the target value.
   251	
   252	\subsection{Realization success}
   253	
   254	A branch realizes the framework when the actual moving-throat solution lands on the target packet.  For example, a branch may have the correct algebraic response framework but still fail the normalization condition, the orbit-lock condition, the selected-support condition, or a same-charge admissibility gate.  That failure is a realization failure, not a failure of the algebraic compiler.
   255	
   256	\subsection{Closure failure}
   257	
   258	A closure fails when the assumptions under which a result was derived are not satisfied.  For example, a formula derived on an isotropic grouped real \(P_2\) branch cannot be applied unchanged to an anisotropic branch without carrying the anisotropy defects.  A rigid-mouth theorem does not automatically apply to a non-rigid mouth branch.  A strict conservative result does not automatically include leakage, work, or export terms from the relaxed open-system extension.
   259	
   260	These distinctions are not rhetorical.  They determine how future papers are allowed to cite this companion.
   261	
   262	\section{Claim-status discipline}
   263	
   264	The status tags used throughout the ledger have the following purpose in this chapter.
   265	
   266	\begin{longtable}{L{0.25\textwidth}L{0.68\textwidth}}
   267	\toprule
   268	Status tag & Meaning for the purpose and scope of this document \\
   269	\midrule
   270	\endhead
   271	\StatusExact & The claim follows from the declared parent action, an exact definition, an exact identity, or exact algebra once the variables and conventions are fixed. \\
   272	\addlinespace
   273	\StatusExactClosure & The claim is exact inside a stated closure family, branch class, gauge convention, search class, or reduced hierarchy.  It is not thereby an unconditional theorem of the full PDE. \\
   274	\addlinespace
   275	\StatusReduced & The claim requires a controlled reduction, low-frequency expansion, normal-mode truncation, projection, selected branch, small-body limit, or other declared ansatz. \\
   276	\addlinespace
   277	\StatusEffective & The claim uses a physically motivated closure that has not yet been uniquely derived from the completed moving-throat PDE. \\
   278	\addlinespace
   279	\StatusNumerical & The object is defined sharply but the currently known placement or value is obtained by numerical solve or numerical search rather than by closed-form expression. \\
   280	\addlinespace
   281	\StatusOpen & The claim depends on actual branch realization or on a PDE-side datum not yet derived or verified in the completed branch. \\
   282	\bottomrule
   283	\end{longtable}
   284	
   285	Every theorem block in the final ledger should state its status before the proof is read.  The status tag is part of the claim.
   286	
   287	\section{What counts as verification}
   288	
   289	Verification in this ledger does not mean that every line is independently re-derived from the parent action in every chapter.  It means that the chain of dependency is explicit enough that a reader can audit it.
   290	
   291	A verified stage should provide at least one of the following forms of support.
   292	
   293	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2.2em]
   294	  \item \textbf{Direct variation or algebra.}  The result follows by varying the declared action, eliminating a quadratic block, projecting a mode equation, expanding a rational response, or performing an exact symbolic manipulation shown in the text.
   295	  \item \textbf{Controlled reduction with stated assumptions.}  The result follows after a declared low-frequency, finite-throat, small-body, stable-mode, isotropic, passive/outgoing, rigid-mouth, or selected-support reduction.
   296	  \item \textbf{Symbolic audit.}  The result is backed by a script that checks identities, projectors, expansions, ranks, nullspaces, roots, or finite candidate sets.
   297	  \item \textbf{Numerical location with exact target.}  The target equation or optimization problem is exact, while the realized value is numerical.
   298	  \item \textbf{No-go by exhaustion inside a declared class.}  The result rules out a branch, mechanism, or search class only after the class has been explicitly defined.
   299	\end{enumerate}
   300	
   301	The ledger should not use the word ``verified'' for an intuition, analogy, or desired branch behavior that has not passed one of these tests.
   302	
   303	\subsection{Verification routing}
   304	
   305	The stage number is the paper-facing verification handle.  To keep the archive
   306	readable, the PDF does not print the full script filename inventory inside every
   307	stage card.
   308	
   309	All paths below are relative to \nolinkurl{research/pde_ledger/}.  The audit
   310	layer is routed by naming convention.
   311	\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2.2em]
   312	  \item SymPy symbolic audits live under \nolinkurl{scripts/} and follow the
   313	  pattern
   314	  \nolinkurl{moving_throat_pde_stageNNN_*_sympy_audit.py}.
   315	  \item Mathematica symbolic audits live under
   316	  \nolinkurl{mathematica/} and follow the pattern
   317	  \nolinkurl{moving_throat_pde_stageNNN_*_mathematica_audit.wl}.
   318	  \item Numerical stress harnesses live under \nolinkurl{scripts/numerical/}
   319	  and \nolinkurl{mathematica/numerical/}, usually with names of
   320	  the form \nolinkurl{stageNNN*_stress.py} and
   321	  \nolinkurl{stageNNN*_stress.wl}.  Shared harnesses may cover short ranges as
   322	  \nolinkurl{stage003_021_*}.
   323	  \item The exact path inventory, coverage counts, and trust classification are
   324	  maintained in repo-level verification trackers rather than repeated inside the
   325	  paper.
   326	\end{itemize}

   328	\section{How this companion should be used by future papers}
   329	
   330	Future papers should cite this companion in two different ways.
   331	
   332	\subsection{Citing a theorem anchor}
   333	
   334	When a future paper needs a stable mathematical result, it should cite the theorem anchor.  Examples include:
   335	\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2.2em]
   336	  \item the moving-surface lift and collective recovery of \(a,L\),
   337	  \item the grouped real \(P_2\) projector calculus,
   338	  \item the outgoing quadrupole normalization bridge,
   339	  \item the weak-axisymmetric orbit/quotient theorem,
   340	  \item the finite mixed-ray realization sieve,
   341	  \item the rigid-mouth Cartesian orbit-lock theorem,
   342	  \item the relaxed barrier/export compiler.
   343	\end{itemize}
   344	
   345	The theorem anchor should carry the claim status and the stage range.
   346	
   347	\subsection{Citing a provenance stage}
   348	
   349	When a future paper needs to show where an intermediate formula came from, it should cite the stage or stage range.  Stage citations are especially appropriate for long overlap calculations, symbolic-audit outputs, no-go filters, numerical placements, or branch-specific construction details.
   350	
   351	\subsection{Citing an open gap}
   352	
   353	When a future paper relies on a still-open branch datum, it should cite the relevant open packet directly rather than burying it in prose.  For example, it should say that it assumes or tests the actual branch value of \(\widehat m_0^{\,2}P_0\), \(\Xi_1\), the rigid-mouth \((U,V)\) packet, the selected twin-support coordinate, or the relaxed leakage/export packet, as appropriate.
   354	
   355	\section{Scope boundaries}
   356	
   357	The ledger includes the derivation of the moving-throat response framework and the stage sequence through the relaxed open-system extension.  It does not attempt to do all future work at once.  The following boundaries are intentional.
   358	
   359	\subsection{No replacement of the parent papers}
   360	
   361	This document imports the parent action, corrected charge ontology, projection/reduction distinction, and lower-order PN assembly results.  It does not rewrite those papers from scratch.  Where a parent identity is needed, this companion should restate only the amount required to make the moving-throat derivation self-contained.
   362	
   363	\subsection{No assumption-free claim of a solved nonlinear PDE}
   364	
   365	The ledger derives the response machinery and branch tests.  It does not claim that the full nonlinear moving-throat PDE has been solved in closed form.  Actual branch realization remains a separate task whenever the status tag says \StatusOpen, \StatusNumerical, \StatusEffective, or \StatusExactClosure.
   366	
   367	\subsection{No hiding of branch restrictions}
   368	
   369	The ledger should not state an isotropic result as if it were anisotropic, a rigid-mouth result as if it were non-rigid, a selected-support result as if it were generic, or a strict conservative result as if it already contained the relaxed leakage/work/export extension.
   370

     1	\chapter{Claim-Status Firewall}
     2	\label{chap:claim-status-firewall}
     3	
     4	This chapter fixes the claim-status rules for the entire derivation ledger.  The moving-throat program contains several different kinds of mathematical statements: exact identities of the declared parent theory, exact algebra inside reduced closures, controlled reductions, effective closure choices, numerical placements, and open branch-realization targets.  These categories are not interchangeable.  The purpose of the claim-status firewall is to make that separation visible everywhere the ledger states a result.
     5	
     6	The firewall should be read as part of the mathematics of the document, not as editorial decoration.  A theorem that is exact only inside a closure is not an exact theorem of the full nonlinear moving-throat PDE.  A compiler that reduces a branch test to finite observables is not the same thing as a proof that the actual branch realizes those observables.  A numerically located point is not a closed-form value merely because the equations defining it are exact.  An open target remains open even if all algebra leading to the target is exact.
     7	
     8	\begin{quote}
     9	The status tag attached to a result states the strongest honest way that result may be cited.
    10	\end{quote}
    11	
    12	Every theorem, proposition, lemma, boxed equation, branch verdict, no-go statement, finite search result, and stage output in this companion must carry one of the status tags defined below.
    13	
    14	\section{The six allowed status tags}
    15	\label{sec:six-status-tags}
    16	
    17	The ledger uses exactly six status tags.  These tags are intentionally coarse.  The goal is not to encode every nuance in the tag itself; the goal is to prevent the most dangerous mistakes: treating reduced results as exact, treating closures as solved PDE branches, treating numerical locations as closed-form derivations, or treating open branch targets as completed theorems.
    18	
    19	\begin{longtable}{L{0.23\textwidth}L{0.68\textwidth}}
    20	\toprule
    21	Status tag & Meaning \\
    22	\midrule
    23	\endhead
    24	\StatusExact & The statement follows directly from the declared parent action, exact definitions, exact identities, exact variational equations, or exact algebra with no additional branch ansatz beyond the stated definitions. \\
    25	\addlinespace
    26	\StatusExactClosure & The statement is exact inside a stated reduced closure family, branch, hierarchy, search class, or ansatz.  The algebra inside the closure is exact, but the closure itself is not thereby promoted to an unconditional theorem of the completed PDE. \\
    27	\addlinespace
    28	\StatusReduced & The statement follows after a controlled reduction, such as a projection, zero-mode limit, low-frequency expansion, small-body/worldtube approximation, finite-mode truncation, selected-branch restriction, isotropic branch assumption, passive/outgoing reduction, or asymptotic regime. \\
    29	\addlinespace
    30	\StatusEffective & The statement uses a physically motivated closure choice, modeling ansatz, constitutive packet, or branch prescription that is useful and internally coherent but not yet uniquely forced by the completed moving-throat PDE. \\
    31	\addlinespace
    32	\StatusNumerical & The defining equations are exact or closure-exact, but the reported value, branch point, candidate, finite placement, or search output is currently known through numerical solve, numerical scan, or numerical localization rather than closed-form derivation. \\
    33	\addlinespace
    34	\StatusOpen & The statement still depends on actual branch realization, a PDE-side existence or uniqueness theorem, a not-yet-computed overlap, a not-yet-verified normalization, or another result not completed in the current ledger. \\
    35	\bottomrule
    36	\end{longtable}
    37	
    38	These tags are mutually exclusive for a single atomic claim.  A paragraph may contain several claims with different statuses; in that case the paragraph must either split the claims or explicitly state the status of each part.

    45	verification evidence is attached to a stage, value, or audit record.  An audit

    48	But the same-charge barrier / support-selection side of the program still carried one scalar ambiguity:
    49	
    50	\[
    51	\varrho=\frac{\pi^2\Pi_{\rm tr}}{16\Lambda}.
    52	\]
    53	
    54	What was still missing was the actual value selected by the passive/outgoing normalization side.
    55	This stage fixes that value exactly by combining two already-carried ingredients:
    56	
    57	1. the selected-branch product identities, which cancel all separate outgoing-normalization amplitudes and reduce the support test to a single loading ratio,
    58	2. the minimal isotropic conservative quadrupole precursor, whose contact/pole split fixes that loading ratio algebraically.
    59	
    60	So the real job of Stage 240 is:
    61	
    62	> compress the selected-branch support demand from an open scalar selector down to one exact support slice.
    63	
    64	---
    65	
    66	## Provenance
    67	
    68	This note is the moving-throat Stage-240 version of the support-selection computation carried by the selected-branch normalization track.
    69	The barrier-audit Stage 142 records the same result in the same notation, and the matching `g2` step carries the exact contact-plus-pole extraction that fixes the loading ratio.
    70	
    71	---
    72	
    73	## 0. Why this stage is needed
    74	
    75	Before this step, the selected passive/outgoing support problem was still phrased in terms of the demand parameter
    76	
    77	\[
    78	\varrho=\frac{\pi^2\Pi_{\rm tr}}{16\Lambda},
    79	\]
    80	
    81	with three possible support regimes:
    82	
    83	\[
    84	\Pi_{\rm tr}\le C_{\rm mix}
    85	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    86	\text{mixed-only enough},
    87	\]
    88	
    89	\[
    90	C_{\rm mix}<\Pi_{\rm tr}\le 2C_{\rm mix}
    91	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    92	\text{symmetric lowest twin enough},
    93	\]
    94	
    95	\[
    96	\Pi_{\rm tr}>2C_{\rm mix}
    97	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    98	\text{non-twin asymmetry required}.
    99	\]
   100	
   101	So the missing datum was no longer a whole response function.
   102	It was only the exact ratio \(\Pi_{\rm tr}/C_{\rm mix}\) selected by the passive/outgoing branch.
   103	
   104	This stage shows that the ratio is not free.
   105	
   106	---
   107	
   108	## 1. Exact selected-branch product identities
   109	
   110	The selected-branch normalization side gives the exact product formulas
   111	
   112	\[
   113	\Pi_{\rm tr}
   114	=
   115	\frac{N_Q^{(\rm target)}}{\beta_0}\,\alpha_{\rm req},
   116	\qquad
   117	C_{\rm mix}
   118	=
   119	\frac{N_Q^{(\rm target)}}{\beta_0}\,\alpha_{\rm mix}.
   120	\]
   121	
   122	Therefore the separate selected-mode amplitudes cancel immediately in the ratio:
   123	
   124	\[
   125	\boxed{
   126	\frac{\Pi_{\rm tr}}{C_{\rm mix}}
   127	=
   128	\frac{\alpha_{\rm req}}{\alpha_{\rm mix}}
   129	=:\rho_\alpha.
   130	}
   131	\]
   132	
   133	So the selected support demand depends only on the loading ratio
   134	
   135	\[
   136	\boxed{
   137	\rho_\alpha:=\frac{\alpha_{\rm req}}{\alpha_{\rm mix}}.
   138	}
   139	\]
   140	
   141	In the spectral notation of the selected branch one may also write
   142	
   143	\[
   144	N_Q^{(\rm target)}
   145	=
   146	\hat m_-^{\,2}\,\beta_0\,\frac{s_-}{\lambda_-},
   147	\]
   148	
   149	so the same identities become
   150	
   151	\[
   152	\Pi_{\rm tr}
   153	=
   154	\hat m_-^{\,2}\frac{s_-}{\lambda_-}\alpha_{\rm req},
   155	\qquad
   156	C_{\rm mix}
   157	=
   158	\hat m_-^{\,2}\frac{s_-}{\lambda_-}\alpha_{\rm mix},
   159	\]
   160	
   161	and again the ratio is exactly \(\rho_\alpha\).
   162	
   163	So after the selected-branch normalization is imposed, the support test no longer scans independent amplitudes.
   164	It scans one loading ratio.
   165	
   166	---
   167	
   168	## 2. Exact contact-plus-pole inverse compiler
   169	
   170	Write the natural minimal conservative quadrupole precursor as
   171	
   172	\[
   173	Y_Q^{\rm cons}(\omega)
   174	=
   175	c_0+\frac{c_1}{1-\omega^2/\Omega_Q^2},
   176	\qquad
   177	c_0+c_1=1.
   178	\]
   179	
   180	On the explicit support/source branch the natural contact/pole interpretation is:
   181	
   182	- the mixed baseline contributes the static contact fraction,
   183	- the extra support lane contributes the finite conservative pole.
   184	
   185	So the same precursor can be written as
   186	
   187	\[
   188	Y_Q^{\rm cons}(\omega)
   189	=
   190	\frac{\alpha_{\rm mix}}{\alpha_{\rm req}}
   191	+
   192	\frac{\alpha_{\rm req}-\alpha_{\rm mix}}{\alpha_{\rm req}}
   193	\frac{1}{1-\omega^2/\Omega_Q^2}.
   194	\]
   195	
   196	Introducing the loading ratio
   197	\[
   198	\rho_\alpha:=\frac{\alpha_{\rm req}}{\alpha_{\rm mix}},
   199	\]
   200	this becomes
   201	\[
   202	Y_Q^{\rm cons}(\omega)
   203	=
   204	\frac{1}{\rho_\alpha}
   205	+
   206	\frac{\rho_\alpha-1}{\rho_\alpha}
   207	\frac{1}{1-\omega^2/\Omega_Q^2}.
   208	\]
   209	
   210	So the contact and pole fractions are exactly
   211	
   212	\[
   213	\boxed{
   214	c_0=\frac{1}{\rho_\alpha},
   215	\qquad
   216	c_1=\frac{\rho_\alpha-1}{\rho_\alpha}.
   217	}
   218	\]
   219	
   220	The inverse formulas are therefore immediate:
   221	
   222	\[
   223	\boxed{
   224	\rho_\alpha=\frac{1}{c_0}=\frac{1}{1-c_1},
   225	}
   226	\]
   227	
   228	and
   229	
   230	\[
   231	\boxed{
   232	\zeta_{\rm req}:=\rho_\alpha-1=\frac{c_1}{c_0}.
   233	}
   234	\]
   235	
   236	So the support/source loading ratio is encoded exactly in the static contact/pole split of the conservative quadrupole precursor.
   237	
   238	### 2.1 What does not matter here
   239	
   240	The pole location \(\Omega_Q\) controls the dynamical conservative shape of the precursor, but it does **not** enter the static loading-ratio extraction.
   241	At this stage only the normalized contact and pole weights \((c_0,c_1)\) matter.
   242	
   243	That is why the support-selection problem collapses so sharply.
   244	
   245	---
   246	
   247	## 3. Matching to the minimal isotropic quadrupole module
   248	
   249	The minimal isotropic conservative quadrupole module is
   250	
   251	\[
   252	\boxed{
   253	c_0=\frac34,
   254	\qquad
   255	c_1=\frac14,
   256	\qquad
   257	\Omega_Q=\frac{3c_s}{2a}.
   258	}
   259	\]
   260	
   261	Substituting these values into the inverse compiler gives immediately
   262	
   263	\[
   264	\boxed{
   265	\rho_\alpha=\frac{1}{3/4}=\frac43,
   266	}
   267	\]
   268	
   269	and
   270	
   271	\[
   272	\boxed{
   273	\zeta_{\rm req}=\frac{1/4}{3/4}=\frac13.
   274	}
   275	\]
   276	
   277	Then the selected demand product is fixed exactly:
   278	
   279	\[
   280	\boxed{

    35	    if simplified != 0:
    36	        raise AssertionError(f"{label} failed: {simplified}")

    38	
    39

   312	\]

   322	\]
   323
